thread:
anya: Heads up — seeing a sharp spike in tiny-gpu job evictions in ap-southeast1 starting ~08:10 UTC. ~1.8k preempts in 30m.
anya: Most victims are short-lived training pods (req: 1g, 1gpu) that should be warm-pool eligible.
anya: Node logs show repeated conntrack exhaustion and warm-pool drain cycles.

sam: looking now — my heatmap shows concentrated evictions on rack nodes with label `az=apse1-b`. Link: https://grafana/redwood/d/evict/evict-heat
sam: scheduler rollout 2026-03-18 changed topology scoring weights; could be packing sensitivity change.

maria: quick raw snippet from scheduler log:
```text
I03/21 08:12:43 scheduler.go:523] preempt: chosen victim pod=training-mini-123 node=gpu-node-07 scoreDelta=22 reason=taint(packed=true:NoSchedule)
I03/21 08:12:44 kubelet.go:321] eviction: pod training-mini-123, reclaimed resources=0.5cpu 1Gi
```

tim: pods had toleration for `packed=true` but still got evicted? that suggests eviction path triggered by node pressure rather than scheduling rejection. conntrack + ephemeral disk pressure can cause kubelet to evict regardless of toleration.

opsbot: System alert: 1800 evictions in 30m across ap-southeast1 (nodes: 07,08,09,14) :warning:

eviction-bot: Top evict sources: conntrack (55%), memory-swap (30%), kube-probe-fail (15%).

maria: confirmed — conntrack table fills then kubelet taints node with `node.k8s.io/conntrack-full:NoExecute` then warm-pool drains and scheduler starts chaotic repacks.

sam: rollout suspicion: we lowered `spreadPriority` and bumped `fragmentationPenalty` in the scheduler config last week. That made scheduler more aggressive about binpacking across racks, but with flaky conntrack on some racks it amplifies thrash.

anya: immediate ask: can we stop the churn? proposals:
- revert scheduler sensitivity to previous (sam)
- temporarily disable warm-pool auto-drain for apse1-b nodes (maria)
- run a conservative repack job that moves <=50 pods at a time into cooler racks (tim)
- increase conntrack sysctl on affected nodes as stopgap (ops)

sam: I can roll back the scheduler flag to `fragmentationPenalty: 0.6 -> 0.4` for ap-southeast  to reduce aggressive packing. Patch: `kubectl -n infra patch configmap scheduler-config -p '{"data":{"fragmentationPenalty":"0.4"}}'`

maria: I will patch the warm-pool controller to add `--min-dont-drain-count=10` for the apse1-b pool and set `evictionGrace=60s` so short jobs don't get preempted immediately.

tim: repack job plan: run `repacker:v3` with `--batch-size=50 --prefer-az=apse1-a,apse1-c` target label `gpu-tiny=1`. Command: 
```bash
kubectl run repacker-v3 --image=infra/repacker:latest -- /bin/repack --batch-size=50 --filter 'req.gpu==1 && life<5m' --dest-az 'apse1-a,apse1-c'
```

opsbot: Note: moving pods increases short-term egress and scheduling churn; cost delta estimate ~+3% tokens/hour due to reschedules.

anya: Also long term: need a mitigation in scheduler that penalizes nodes with high conntrack-fill metrics (so placement avoids hotspots). Can we add a metric-weight hook?

sam: that's on the roadmap. Short term I will roll back the sensitivity in 5min and monitor.

maria: I queued the warm-pool patch and will push to canary (apse1-b small pool) now.

tim: I'll prepare and dry-run the repacker, won't execute until you ping me.

anya: thanks all. action items: sam rollback, maria warm-pool patch, tim repack dry-run, ops monitor conntrack and raise sysctl if needed. If we still see >200 evictions/5m after rollback we escalate to a manual drain + reprovision for the worst nodes. :eyes:

sam: rollback complete — scheduler configmap updated. monitoring: https://grafana/redwood/d/evict/evict-heat?var-region=apse1

maria: warm-pool canary applied to apse1-b-pool-2, setting min-dont-drain-count=10.
tim: repacker dry-run ready, waiting for green.

anya: update in 15. thanks. :thumbsup:
